correctness.rationale: Verified for finite nonempty structures with two named equivalences and no other symbols, with comparisons restricted to that class. The intersection matrix is a complete isomorphism invariant modulo independent row and column permutations. Removing one element reverses one of the four extensions; the orbit selector fixes invariant column sums, examines every within-group order, and sorts rows. Counting refinement uses the four ordered relation channels and previous colors; equality is recovered by splitting out exactly one point of the current color from the (1,1) channel. Unary color formulas follow by counting quantifiers, and induction on formulas using the atomic pair type and endpoint colors gives completeness of the stabilized color histograms. Different cardinalities are distinguishable by a counting sentence. A separate reproduction fixing one partition by block sizes and generating every second partition by restricted-growth strings, followed by synchronized refinement, gave iso counts 1,4,10,33,91,298,910,3017 and logical counts 1,4,10,33,91,298,910,3016. It found just the displayed two matrices in the non-singleton class at eight. The pair is nonisomorphic by incidence connectivity and has identical uniform profiles (1,1,1,5), so its equivalence also follows without the census. value.rationale: A natural relational class already has a known orbit count and a natural logical invariant. Determining precisely when that invariant ceases to distinguish types, and showing the known matching fibre is the sole discrepancy among all 3,017 types at the first order, gives an independently useful obstruction and exact test benchmark. It is not merely recomputing the known orbit column or confirming the matching example.
